name: mobile
//port: Metro runs on 8082, not its default 8081.
8081 is a crowded port — Apache ships on it in several bundles (XAMPP, and the httpd
inside EDB Postgres Enterprise Manager), and Metro loses that fight silently rather
than loudly: it binds [::] in dual-stack mode, so a rival bound to 0.0.0.0:8081 takes
IPv4 while Metro keeps IPv6. A phone or emulator then reaches the wrong server and
reports 'Failed to download remote update', which points at nothing useful.
Moving off 8081 costs nothing and removes the whole class of problem.
web:pkce is deliberately NOT moved — see its own note below.

scripts.//start:clear: Same as start, with Metro's transform cache cleared. Exists because the bare `npx expo start -c` silently falls back to port 8081 — see the port note above and Problem 1 in the README.
scripts.//web:pkce: Port 5173 is not cosmetic — it is the callback already registered on the Cognito web client, so AUTH_MODE=cognito-pkce works here with no infrastructure change.
scripts.build: expo export --platform ios && expo export --platform android
scripts.//test: jest-expo preset: transforms the RN/Expo module graph that plain jest cannot parse. --ci in CI keeps snapshots from being written silently.
scripts.//test:coverage: Writes coverage/lcov.info, which sonar-project.properties points at. Sonar reads coverage from that file - it does not run tests itself.
scripts.//check:locales: Fails when a locale drifts from en.json. A missing key is silent — i18next falls back to English and renders it mid-screen on a safety surface. See scripts/check-locale-parity.mjs.
